Subject: Clarify: private deploy cust keyholder access matrix & geo-exit policy

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We liked the model of a private deployment (VPC) with customer-controlled keys, but legal/security has two specific asks before we proceed:

1) We need a clear access matrix that shows who at Redwood can perform key-holder operations (rotate, revive, or export) and under what authorized trigger (scheduled rotation vs. emergency break-glass). We need this at a role level (operator, infra-oncall, SRE lead) not just a paragraph.

2) We have cross-border concerns: MedNimbus processes EU patient data and can't allow outbound model telemetry or inference payloads to countries outside the EU unless there is a documented geo-exit policy (who can initiate a data export, what approvals are required, and where the copies go).

Can you send a short doc or matrix and clarify whether any Redwood subprocessors would receive plaintext data during normal operations or break-glass? Also please point us to the SOC 2 artifact or where we can validate the control for operator access.

Attached is our DPA annex template with some redlines — legal asked we align on these items before signature.

Best,
Anna

Head of Security, MedNimbus Health

Anna — thanks, and appreciate the redlines. High level answers up front:

- Customer-controlled keys: the customer holds the tenant master key in their KMS; Redwood operators never have the tenant master key in plaintext.
- Operator actions: we can perform operator-led actions (e.g., rotate operator keystore, assist with emergency unseal) only when the customer has explicitly authorized an operator action via a documented break-glass procedure; these actions are logged and require dual-approval from an SRE lead + engineering manager.
- Subprocessors: in private (VPC/on-prem) mode, no Redwood subprocessors receive inference payloads in plaintext. There are cases where we may ship telemetry/metrics aggregated and pseudonymized to our monitoring vendor; that is opt-in and can be disabled in private deployments.

I'm attaching a preliminary access matrix and a visual for the break-glass flow (operator-breakglass-flow.png). Kimberly has more detail on the technical gating and audit trail — adding her into the thread.

Next steps: I'll upload a short annex to the Drive and propose DocuSign for the DPA once we align. If you'd like, propose a 30-min call Monday to walk legal/security through the matrix.

— Jonas
VP, Product & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Anna — quick technical clarifications below, extracted from our private deployment runbook: 

- Key custody: Customer KMS holds tenant master-KEK. Redwood deploys a per-instance wrapping key (RK) that is only present on-host and encrypted with the customer KEK. Operators cannot un-wrap the KEK without a customer-hosted KMS API call.

- Role-level permissions (summary):
  * "Customer Admin": full key operations via customer KMS console/API (rotate, revoke).
  * "Redwood SRE Oncall": can request operator-assist actions; such requests create an immutable ticket and trigger an approval workflow (SRE Lead + Prod Eng Manager) before any operator CLI is executed.
  * "Redwood Security Ops": read-only audit access to telemetry; no ability to export plaintext payloads.
  * "Redwood Platform Engineers": may push software updates; they cannot access tenant secrets without explicit customer-provided unseal authorization.

- Break-glass gating: operator CLI requires a signed customer authorization token (short lived), two Redwood approvers, and the action is recorded to an append-only audit log that is streamed into the customer's logging bucket (or retained in on-prem storage if desired).

- Geo-exit: by default we configure private deploys to restrict egress to the customer's VPC endpoints inside the selected region. Any export request that would cross regional boundaries must pass a policy engine rule: documented reason, legal approval, and a signed export order. We also support a 'no-export' setting which blocks any outbound copies (recommended for PHI).

I'll attach the more detailed XLSX matrix (kms-access-matrix.xlsx) with the exact API calls and log retention windows. If you want us to add column for EU-specific auditors and retention period to match your policy, tell me target retention and we can include.

-Kimberly
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple of follow-ups from Legal/Sec: 

- Can you confirm whether any temporary plaintext access is possible during software updates or migration runs? Legal needs explicit confirmation that rolling updates do not stage plaintext data to Redwood-managed storage.

- For the break-glass flow, legal wants the dual-approval to include a customer delegate (we will provide an enterprise-internal delegate account) in addition to the Redwood approvers for high-sensitivity actions. Is that supported?

- SOC 2: please share the most recent Type II report or a link to the attestation.

If you can answer the three items and push the DPA annex to DocuSign, we can get procurement moving.

Best,
Anna
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Anna — short answers and proposed next steps: 

1) Temporary plaintext during updates: we do not stage plaintext inference payloads to any Redwood-managed storage during rolling updates or migrations for private deployments. Any data that must be transformed in-flight is processed in customer-hosted compute or ephemeral containers that write only to your VPC-backed storage. We will include a clause in the DPA annex to reflect this explicit guarantee.

2) Customer delegate in approval loop: supported. We can configure the approval workflow such that one approver must be a named customer delegate (we'll represent that as a required signer in the break-glass ticket). We'll add that to the access matrix and the annex.

3) SOC 2 link: here is the attestation link — https://status.redwood.ai/soc2-report-2025 (read-only). We'll also include the auditor contact if they need a controlled disclosure.

Action items: Jonas — upload the redlined annex to Drive and kick off DocuSign by EOD. Kimberly — add customer-delegate field to the XLSX and change the export policy text as discussed.

I'll propose Mon 11:00 CET for a 30-min alignment call; please confirm.

— Jonas
